name: Gin & Tonic
notes: Fill the highball with ice before the gin goes in, then pour the tonic down the side. A single slow lift with the spoon mixes it without flattening the bubbles.

name: Vodka Soda
notes: Measure the vodka rather than eyeballing it, since soda water hides nothing. Use a fresh, cold bottle of soda so the drink stays lively to the last sip.

name: Screwdriver
notes: Pour the vodka over ice first and top with orange juice so it mixes on its own. Fresh-squeezed juice makes a noticeable difference over juice from a carton.

name: Cuba Libre
notes: The lime juice is what separates this from an ordinary rum and cola. Add it before the cola, then give one gentle stir so the soda keeps its fizz.

name: Whiskey Ginger
notes: Reach for ginger ale here; ginger beer is spicier and belongs in a mule. Top gently over the whiskey and ice, and squeeze the lime wedge in if the guest wants brightness.

name: Jack & Coke
notes: When a guest names the brand, pour that brand. If it's out of stock, tell them and offer a substitute instead of quietly swapping bottles.

name: Cape Codder
notes: A two-ingredient build, so the ratio matters: keep the cranberry at about twice the vodka. Guests often order it simply as a vodka cranberry.

name: Sea Breeze
notes: Grapefruit is the ingredient that makes it a Sea Breeze; pineapple would make it a Bay Breeze. Pour both juices over the vodka and ice, then stir briefly.

name: Bay Breeze
notes: Pineapple is the tell here, versus grapefruit in the Sea Breeze. Build over ice and give it a quick stir, since pineapple juice tends to settle toward the bottom.

name: Tom Collins
notes: Shake only the gin, lemon, and syrup, strain over fresh ice in the collins glass, then add the soda. Soda in the shaker loses its fizz and can blow the tins apart.

name: Paloma
notes: Put the pinch of salt into the drink itself as well as on the rim; it sharpens the grapefruit. Add the grapefruit soda last and stir just once.

name: Dark 'n' Stormy
notes: Add lime and ginger beer over ice first, then pour the dark rum slowly on top so it sits as a dark layer. Serve unstirred and let the guest mix it.

name: Moscow Mule
notes: Ginger beer brings the bite; ginger ale is too mild for a mule. The copper mug keeps it cold, but the drink works fine in a highball if mugs run out.

name: Kentucky Mule
notes: Built exactly like a Moscow Mule, with bourbon standing in for vodka. Bourbon's sweetness can soften the ginger, so choose a ginger beer with real heat.

name: Margarita
notes: Run lime around only part of the rim before salting, so guests can choose each sip. Shake hard, then strain over fresh cubes rather than the used shaker ice.

name: Daiquiri
notes: Three ingredients leave nowhere to hide, so measure the lime and syrup precisely. Shake hard until the tin is frosty and strain into a chilled coupe with no ice.

name: Whiskey Sour
notes: If the guest wants egg white, shake without ice first to whip it, then add ice and shake again. Without egg, a single hard shake is all it needs.

name: Amaretto Sour
notes: Amaretto is already sweet, so the syrup is cut to a quarter ounce. Adding the full whiskey-sour measure of syrup is the usual way this drink turns cloying.

name: Gimlet
notes: Lime cordial supplies both the sweetness and the acidity, so no separate syrup goes in. Shake hard and serve up in a chilled coupe.

name: Sidecar
notes: Coat just the outer edge of the coupe with sugar so it doesn't fall into the drink. Shake cognac, triple sec, and lemon with ice, then strain with no ice in the glass.

name: Cosmopolitan
garnish: Lime wheel or flamed orange peel
notes: Use a light hand with cranberry; it should turn the drink pink, not dominate it. If flaming the orange peel, hold it well clear of your face and the guest.

name: Lemon Drop
notes: Sugar the rim ahead of time so it dries and stays put. The triple sec adds orange notes that a basic vodka sour lacks, so don't leave it out.

name: Pisco Sour
garnish: Three dashes of bitters drawn through the foam
notes: Dry shake to build the egg-white foam, shake again with ice, and strain into a coupe. Add the bitters to the foam afterward and pull a pick through the drops.

name: Bee's Knees
notes: Make the honey syrup ahead by thinning honey with warm water. Raw honey seizes up when it hits cold ingredients and ends up stuck to the ice.

name: Old Fashioned
notes: Stir the whiskey, syrup, and bitters with ice, then strain over one large cube in the rocks glass. Twist the orange peel over the top so its oils land on the surface.

name: Sazerac
notes: Coat a chilled rocks glass with absinthe and pour out the excess. Stir the rest with ice, strain in neat, then express the lemon peel and discard it.

name: Rusty Nail
notes: Pour scotch and Drambuie straight over the ice in the rocks glass and stir a few times. Drambuie is sweet, so hold back on it rather than overpouring.

name: Dry Martini
notes: Stir, never shake, and keep stirring until it's very cold but not watered down. Ask how dry the guest likes it before you pour the vermouth.

name: Dirty Martini
notes: Ask how dirty the guest likes it and adjust the brine. Use brine from a fresh jar of good olives and stir it with the spirit and vermouth.

name: Gibson
notes: It's made just like a dry martini, but with cocktail onions as the garnish in place of an olive or twist. Serving it with an olive is a common mix-up.

name: Vesper
notes: Unlike most martini-style drinks, this one is shaken. Lillet Blanc takes the place of dry vermouth, so be sure to pour the right bottle.

name: Espresso Martini
notes: Use freshly pulled espresso and shake hard; the crema is what forms the foam on top. Coffee that has cooled and gone stale gives a flat, foamless drink.

name: Manhattan
notes: Stir rather than shake so the texture stays silky and clear. Keep the sweet vermouth in the fridge once opened, because stale vermouth dulls the drink.

name: Rob Roy
notes: Swap the whiskey in a Manhattan for scotch and you have a Rob Roy. A heavily peated scotch can overpower the vermouth, so a milder blend is a safer house pour.

name: Negroni
notes: Measure all three ingredients exactly, stir with ice, and strain over one large cube. Rub the expressed orange peel along the rim before dropping it in.

name: Boulevardier
notes: Pour extra bourbon so the whiskey isn't buried by the Campari and vermouth. Stir and strain over a large cube, then express orange peel over the top.

name: Vieux Carré
notes: Six ingredients go into this one, so set out every bottle before you start. The Bénédictine is only a quarter ounce, and pouring too much makes the drink too sweet.

name: Aperol Spritz
notes: Start with prosecco over ice, add Aperol, and finish with a splash of soda. The Aperol sinks and blends in, so one light stir is plenty.

name: Mimosa
notes: Chill the sparkling wine and the juice so no ice is needed. Pour slowly into a tilted flute to keep foam from running over the rim.

name: Bellini
notes: Put the peach purée into the flute first, then add prosecco slowly while stirring lightly. If you pour too quickly, the purée foams up and spills over.

name: French 75
notes: Shake gin, lemon, and syrup, strain into the flute, then top with champagne. Adding the sparkling wine to the shaker is a mistake that ruins the bubbles.

name: Kir Royale
notes: Put the cassis in first and top with cold champagne; the wine mixes it on the way in. Too much cassis quickly turns it syrupy.

name: Mai Tai
garnish: Mint sprig and spent lime shell
notes: Shake with crushed ice and pour everything into the glass without straining. Tuck the spent lime shell next to the mint sprig for the traditional look.

name: Piña Colada
notes: Blend rum, coconut cream, and pineapple juice with crushed ice until thick but still pourable. Stir the coconut cream well first, since it separates in the can.

name: Painkiller
notes: Shake with crushed ice and pour everything into the glass without straining. Grate fresh nutmeg over the top at the end; pre-ground nutmeg won't have the same aroma.

name: Hurricane
notes: Shake both rums with the passion fruit syrup, lime, and simple syrup, then strain into a hurricane glass filled with fresh cubes. It is a strong drink, so keep the pour measured.

name: Jungle Bird
notes: Campari's bitterness balances the rum and pineapple, so measure it carefully. Shake hard to foam the pineapple juice, then strain over fresh cubes.

name: Mojito
notes: Press the mint lightly with the lime and syrup; shredding the leaves makes the drink bitter. Add rum and crushed ice, then top with a little soda.

name: Caipirinha
notes: Muddle the lime pieces with sugar right in the glass to draw out both juice and peel oil. Add cachaça and crushed ice, and serve without straining.

name: Bloody Mary
notes: Build it in the highball and stir well so the seasonings don't settle at the bottom. Taste it with a straw before garnishing, since tomato juices vary in salt.

name: Long Island Iced Tea
notes: Pour everything except the cola over ice in the highball and stir, then add just a splash of cola. Too much cola hides the sour notes and the drink loses balance.

name: Mint Julep
notes: Muddle the mint gently in the syrup, then add bourbon and pack the cup with crushed ice. Put the mint sprigs right beside the straw so the aroma comes through with each sip.

name: White Russian
notes: Pour vodka and coffee liqueur over ice, then add the cream last. Some guests like it layered and others want it stirred, so ask before stirring it in.

name: Mudslide
notes: Shaking combines the two cream ingredients with the spirits evenly. Drizzle chocolate syrup inside the glass before adding ice so the pattern shows.

name: Brandy Alexander
notes: Shake hard to give the cream a light, airy texture, and strain into a chilled coupe with no ice. Grate nutmeg over the top just before serving.

name: Kamikaze
notes: Vodka, triple sec, and lime go in equal parts. Shake it cold and strain into shot glasses; one shaker batch can serve several people if you scale up evenly.

name: Lemon Drop Shot
notes: Coat the shot glass rim with sugar and dip the lemon wedge in sugar too. Guests drink the shot and bite the lemon right after.

name: Washington Apple
notes: Shake with ice until very cold and strain into the shot glass. Measure the cranberry carefully, because too much makes it taste like juice instead of candy apple.

name: Green Tea Shot
notes: There is no tea in it; the name comes from its pale green color. Shake hard with ice and strain, and use a decent sour mix since it makes up part of the flavor.

name: B-52
notes: Build it heaviest to lightest: coffee liqueur, then Irish cream, then orange liqueur. Pour each over the back of a spoon so the layers stay separate.

name: Michelada
notes: Rim the glass with salt and Tajín, add lime and seasonings over ice, then pour the lager slowly. Pouring the beer too quickly makes it foam over.

name: Irish Coffee
notes: Warm the mug with hot water before building, and stir the sugar into the coffee and whiskey until dissolved. Pour the loosely whipped cream gently over a spoon so it rests on top.

name: Aviation
notes: Measure the violette carefully; a heavy hand makes the drink taste soapy and pushes the color toward purple. Shake hard and strain into a chilled coupe, then express the lemon twist.

name: Clover Club
notes: If using egg white, shake once without ice to foam it, then again with ice. Double-strain so raspberry seeds and ice shards stay out of the coupe.

name: Last Word
notes: All four ingredients go in at the same measure, so jigger each one precisely. A sloppy pour of Chartreuse or maraschino quickly throws off the balance.

name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
notes: Swirl a small amount of absinthe around the chilled coupe and discard the excess before straining in. Too much absinthe will bury the Lillet and orange liqueur.

name: Paper Plane
notes: An equal-parts bourbon sour that relies on Amaro Nonino and Aperol for its bittersweet edge. Substituting a different amaro changes the drink more than you might expect.

name: Southside
notes: Press the mint lightly rather than grinding it, since shredded leaves turn bitter. Double-strain into the coupe so no green flecks end up in the drink.

name: Bramble
notes: Shake the gin, lemon, and syrup, then strain over a mound of crushed ice in a rocks glass. Pour the crème de mûre last so it trickles down through the ice.

name: White Lady
notes: Built like a Sidecar but with gin as the base, so use a clean, dry gin and fresh lemon. Shake well and serve up with no garnish.

name: Between the Sheets
notes: Cognac and white rum share the base with triple sec and lemon in equal measures. It drinks lighter than it is, so pour it as a standard-size serving.

name: Jack Rose
notes: Grenadine made from real pomegranate gives this applejack sour its color and tartness. Bright red commercial syrups mostly add sugar and artificial flavor.

name: Ward 8
notes: Rye whiskey with lemon, a bit of orange juice, and grenadine for sweetness. Keep the grenadine to a quarter ounce, or the drink tips from tart to syrupy.

name: Hemingway Daiquiri
notes: There is no simple syrup here; maraschino provides the only sweetness against lime and grapefruit. Expect a dry, sharp drink, and check the balance before adding sugar.

name: Mary Pickford
notes: Pineapple juice foams nicely when shaken vigorously, giving the drink a light head. Keep the grenadine and maraschino small so the rum and pineapple stay in front.

name: Bacardi Cocktail
notes: Think of it as a Daiquiri that uses grenadine in place of simple syrup, which turns it pink. Use a light, crisp white rum and fresh lime.

name: El Presidente
notes: Stir this one; there is no juice in the recipe, so shaking only clouds it. Use a dry vermouth that is fresh, since an oxidized bottle flattens the drink.

name: Casino
notes: A dry gin sour with only a touch of maraschino and a couple dashes of orange bitters. Keep the lemon measured, since there is no syrup to cushion it.

name: Twentieth Century
notes: Use white crème de cacao, not dark, so the drink stays pale and the cocoa stays in the background. Shake with lemon and Lillet for a crisp finish.

name: Chrysanthemum
notes: Dry vermouth forms the base, so use a fresh, refrigerated bottle. Stir and strain into a chilled coupe; it is a good pick for a guest who wants something lower in alcohol.

name: Bijou
notes: Three equal parts of gin, sweet vermouth, and green Chartreuse, stirred with a dash of orange bitters. Stir long enough for proper dilution, since the Chartreuse is potent.

name: Widow's Kiss
notes: Applejack carries two herbal liqueurs here, so the drink tastes sweet but is quite strong. Stir well for dilution and serve up in a chilled coupe.

name: Remember the Maine
notes: Treat it like a Manhattan with a quarter ounce of cherry liqueur and an absinthe-rinsed glass. Stir the rest, then strain into the rinsed, chilled coupe.

name: Blood and Sand
notes: Because it contains orange juice, this equal-parts Scotch drink is shaken rather than stirred. Fresh orange juice makes a noticeable difference over carton juice.

name: Monkey Gland
notes: Gin and orange juice sweetened with a little grenadine, plus two dashes of absinthe. Keep the absinthe to dashes; it should add depth without dominating.

name: Corpse Reviver No. 1
notes: Unlike the gin-based No. 2, this version has no citrus. Stir the cognac, calvados, and sweet vermouth until cold and strain into a chilled coupe.

name: Pink Lady
notes: Gin, grenadine, and lemon, with optional egg white for body. If you add the egg, shake without ice first to build foam, then shake again with ice.

name: Caipiroska
notes: Muddle lime pieces with sugar in the rocks glass to release juice and peel oils, then add vodka and crushed ice. Avoid mashing the white pith too hard.

name: Caipirissima
notes: Handle it like a Caipirinha: press the lime with sugar in the glass, add white rum, and pack with crushed ice. Stir to dissolve any leftover sugar.

name: Ti' Punch
notes: Press a lime wedge in the glass with a little cane syrup to release its juice and oils, then add the agricole rhum. It is served without ice, so the spirit stays front and center.

name: Batida
notes: Blend the cachaça, coconut cream, condensed milk, and lime with crushed ice until smooth. Go easy on the condensed milk; it sweetens quickly.

name: Pisco Punch
notes: The pineapple gum syrup is the key ingredient and has to be made ahead of time. Shake it with pisco and lime, and strain into a chilled coupe.

name: Rum Punch
notes: Shake the rum with orange, pineapple, lime, and grenadine, then strain into a hurricane glass over fresh cubed ice. Taste the juices first, since their sweetness varies.

name: Planter's Punch
notes: Shake the dark rum, lime, syrup, and bitters, strain over ice in a collins glass, and finish with soda. Add the soda last so it keeps its fizz.

name: Queen's Park Swizzle
notes: Muddle the mint gently in the glass, add rum, lime, and syrup, then fill with crushed ice and churn with a swizzle stick. Dash the bitters on top to form a layer.

name: Corn 'n' Oil
notes: Build it over cubed ice in a rocks glass and give it a short stir. Blackstrap rum is heavy and molasses-rich, so the falernum and lime are there to lift it.

name: Piscola
notes: Pour pisco over ice in a highball glass and top with cola. The ratio is a matter of taste, so ask the guest how strong they want it.

name: Cantarito
notes: Salt the rim before building, then add tequila, citrus juices, and a pinch of salt over ice. Top with grapefruit soda last and stir gently once.

name: Ranch Water
notes: Build tequila and lime over ice in a highball and top with a crisp, highly carbonated soda water. Its appeal is how dry and light it is, so skip any sweetener.

name: Batanga
notes: Salt the rim, add tequila, lime, and salt over ice, then top with cola. Stir gently so the carbonation survives.

name: Chilcano
notes: Build the pisco and lime over ice, top with ginger ale, and finish with bitters. Ginger ale keeps it softer and less spicy than a drink made with ginger beer.

name: Rum Swizzle
notes: Combine the rum, lime, syrup, and bitters over crushed ice and spin a swizzle stick until the glass frosts. Finish with a short splash of soda.

name: Suffering Bastard
notes: Shake the gin, brandy, lime, and bitters, strain into a collins glass over ice, and top with ginger beer. Don't shake the ginger beer, or it will lose its fizz.

name: Fish House Punch
notes: Rum, cognac, and peach brandy form a strong base, so taste for balance when making a big batch. Chill the punch bowl ahead of time and keep it well stocked with cubed ice.

name: Trinidad Sour
notes: The Angostura really is poured by the ounce; rye plays only a supporting role. Orgeat and lemon tame the bitterness, so measure them accurately.

name: Doctor Funk
notes: Shake the dark rum, lime, grenadine, and absinthe, strain into a collins glass over ice, and top with soda. Keep the absinthe to two dashes.

name: Hotel Nacional Special
notes: White rum and pineapple get depth from apricot liqueur and a sharp edge from lime. Shake hard for a frothy texture and serve up in a coupe.

name: Penicillin
notes: Shake the blended Scotch, lemon, and honey-ginger syrup, strain over ice, then gently float the Islay malt on top. Don't stir after floating.

name: Gold Rush
notes: Honey syrup replaces simple syrup in this bourbon sour. Thin the honey with warm water first, since straight honey seizes up on contact with cold ice.

name: Naked & Famous
notes: An equal-parts shaken drink of mezcal, Aperol, yellow Chartreuse, and lime. Choose a mezcal that isn't overly smoky, or it will flatten the other three.

name: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
notes: Reposado tequila carries the drink; the half ounce of mezcal is there for smoky accent. Stir over ice, strain onto a large cube, and express orange peel over the top.

name: Kentucky Buck
notes: Build the bourbon, lemon, and bitters over ice in a copper mug and top with ginger beer. Add the strawberry garnish last so it doesn't sink.

name: Tommy's Margarita
notes: This version has no orange liqueur; agave syrup sweetens it and lets the tequila come through. Shake and strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.

name: Brooklyn
notes: A rye and dry vermouth drink with maraschino and a couple of dashes of amaro. Since the traditional amer is hard to find, pick a bittersweet, orange-leaning amaro.

name: Greenpoint
notes: Close in structure to a Manhattan, with sweet vermouth and a quarter ounce of yellow Chartreuse. Stir, strain into a coupe, and use a lemon twist rather than a cherry.

name: Elder Fashioned
notes: St-Germain takes the place of sugar, so don't add extra sweetener. Stir with bitters and strain over a large cube, then express the lemon twist over the glass.

name: Gin Gin Mule
notes: Shake the gin, lime, syrup, and mint, then strain into a highball over fresh ice and top with ginger beer. Double-strain to keep mint bits out.

name: Hugo Spritz
notes: Press the mint lightly in the wine glass, add ice and elderflower liqueur, then pour the prosecco and a splash of soda. Stir gently to keep the bubbles.

name: Whiskey Smash
notes: Muddle the lemon wedges and mint firmly to release juice and peel oils, then add bourbon and syrup over crushed ice. The peel oils give it more depth than juice alone.

name: Mezcal Negroni
notes: Equal parts mezcal, Campari, and sweet vermouth, stirred and strained over a large cube. A milder mezcal keeps the smoke from overwhelming the Campari.

name: Cable Car
notes: Prepare the cinnamon-sugar rim before shaking so the drink goes out cold. Spiced rum and orange curaçao with lemon make it a Sidecar-style sour.

name: Final Ward
notes: Four equal measures, but rye and lemon replace the gin and lime of a Last Word. Shake hard and double strain into a chilled coupe; the rye should still come through the Chartreuse.

name: Bitter Giuseppe
notes: An amaro-forward stirred drink with Cynar as the base instead of a spirit. The small squeeze of lemon brightens it, so stir briefly and keep it cold.

name: Air Mail
notes: Shake only the rum, lime and honey syrup, strain into the flute, then add champagne last. Thin stiff honey with warm water first or it will clump in the shaker.

name: Pegu Club
notes: A gin sour sharpened with curaçao and both Angostura and orange bitters. Keep the lime at half an ounce so the curaçao and bitters are not buried; serve up in a chilled coupe.

name: Death in the Afternoon
notes: Put the absinthe in the flute first, then add well-chilled champagne a little at a time. The mix clouds as the wine goes in, and a slow pour keeps it from foaming over.

name: Kingston Negroni
notes: Stir with ice and strain over one large cube, then express orange peel on top. A mild white rum gets lost against Campari, so reach for a pungent Jamaican bottle.

name: Buttery Nipple
notes: Butterscotch schnapps goes in first because it is heavier; ease the Irish cream on top off the back of a spoon. Pour too fast and the two blur together.

name: Alabama Slammer
notes: Four half-ounce parts, shaken briefly with ice and strained into a shot glass. Remember sloe gin is a sweet plum-like liqueur, which gives the shot its red tint.

name: Jäger Bomb
notes: Pour the energy drink into the rocks glass without ice, then drop in a shot of cold Jägermeister. Use a sturdy glass and leave headroom so it does not splash out.

name: Red Headed Slut
notes: Keep the peach schnapps, cranberry and Jägermeister cold and shake them only briefly before straining. Equal half-ounce parts; the fruit juice softens the herbal liqueur.

name: Slippery Nipple
notes: Sambuca sits on the bottom, with Irish cream laid gently over it using a spoon. Same technique as a Buttery Nipple, but with an anise base instead of butterscotch.

name: Mind Eraser
notes: Start with ice in the rocks glass, add vodka, float coffee liqueur carefully, then top with soda so the layers stay apart. Serve with a straw so it is sipped from the bottom.

name: Cement Mixer
notes: Pour the Irish cream, then add the lime juice right before serving. The acid curdles the cream almost immediately, which is the intended effect, so tell the guest what to expect.

name: Duck Fart
notes: Coffee liqueur goes down first, Irish cream is spooned over it, and the Crown Royal is floated on top. Pour each layer slowly so the whisky stays on the surface.

name: Surfer on Acid
notes: Shake the Jägermeister, coconut rum and pineapple juice hard with ice and strain. A good shake gives the pineapple a light foam on top of the shot.

name: Three Wise Men
notes: Build equal parts of the three named whiskeys straight into the shot glass with no ice or mixer. Nothing hides a bad pour here, so measure each part.

name: Woo Woo
notes: Equal parts vodka, peach schnapps and cranberry, shaken with ice and strained. If it tastes syrupy, the cranberry is probably a sweetened cocktail blend rather than juice.

name: Melon Ball
notes: Shake the vodka, Midori and pineapple juice with ice and strain into a shot glass. Chill it well, since a warm melon liqueur shot tastes cloying.

name: Blow Job
notes: Pour the Irish cream and butterscotch schnapps into the shot glass, then finish with a small dome of whipped cream. Add the cream right before handing it over.

name: Chocolate Cake Shot
notes: Shake the vodka and Frangelico with ice and strain. Hand it over with a lemon wedge rolled in sugar; the guest bites the lemon right after the shot.

name: Pickleback
notes: Pour two separate shots, one of Irish whiskey and one of pickle brine, served side by side. Chill the brine and use a clean, plain dill brine rather than a sweet one.

name: Zombie
notes: Shake everything, including the dash of absinthe, and pour over crushed ice in a tiki mug. It carries four ounces of rum, so consider a one-per-guest limit.

name: Scorpion Bowl
notes: Shake the rum, brandy, juices and orgeat, then pour over crushed ice in the bowl with several straws. Use the batch scaler to multiply servings instead of guessing ratios.

name: Navy Grog
notes: Three rums balanced by lime, grapefruit and honey syrup, shaken and poured over crushed ice. Warm the honey syrup slightly if it has thickened so it blends evenly.

name: Fog Cutter
notes: Shake the three spirits with orange, lemon and orgeat, pour over crushed ice, then float the sherry on top. It is stronger than its juice-heavy taste suggests.

name: Three Dots and a Dash
garnish: Three brandied cherries and a pineapple spear
notes: The garnish spells the name: three cherries and one pineapple spear on a pick, like the Morse letter V. Shake the rest and serve over crushed ice in a tiki mug.

name: Beachcomber
notes: Essentially a Daiquiri boosted with triple sec and a little maraschino. Go easy on the maraschino, as a quarter ounce is plenty; shake and serve up without ice.

name: Missionary's Downfall
notes: Add the mint leaves directly to the blender with the other ingredients and crushed ice, and blend until the mint is fine and the drink is smooth. Pour into a hurricane glass.

name: Saturn
notes: A gin-based tiki drink using passion fruit, orgeat and falernum. Shake hard, strain into a chilled coupe with no ice, and twist a lemon peel over the top.

name: Test Pilot
notes: Shake the aged and overproof rum together with lime, falernum, curaçao and bitters, then pour over crushed ice. Measure the overproof carefully since it adds a lot of strength.

name: 151 Swizzle
notes: Combine the ingredients in the collins glass over crushed ice and work them together with a swizzle stick or barspoon until the glass frosts. Top with more ice as it settles.

name: Bahama Mama
notes: Shake the rums, orange and pineapple juice and grenadine together, then pour over crushed ice. Easy to scale up by the pitcher for a group.

name: Blue Hawaii
notes: Blend everything with crushed ice until smooth. Blue curaçao is an orange liqueur, so the color is striking but the flavor stays citrus, pineapple and coconut.

name: Chi-Chi
notes: Blend vodka, coconut cream and pineapple juice with crushed ice until thick. Mix the coconut cream before measuring, as it separates in the can.

name: Singapore Sling
notes: Shake everything except the soda, strain over cubed ice in a collins glass, and finish with soda. Measure the quarter-ounce liqueurs precisely; small changes shift the balance.

name: Jet Pilot
notes: Shake all the rums with the juices, falernum, cinnamon syrup and absinthe, then pour over crushed ice. Grapefruit and cinnamon are what set it apart from a Test Pilot.

name: Americano
notes: Campari and sweet vermouth in equal parts over ice, lengthened with soda. Think of it as a lighter, bubbly Negroni with soda where the gin would be.

name: John Collins
notes: Shake the bourbon, lemon and simple syrup, strain over fresh ice in a collins glass, and top with soda. Add the soda after straining so it keeps its fizz.

name: Horse's Neck
notes: Peel a lemon in one unbroken spiral and hang it inside the highball before adding ice. Then pour the bourbon and top with ginger ale.

name: Shirley Temple
notes: Fill the highball with ice and ginger ale, then pour the grenadine in last so it drifts down through the glass. Add the cherry on top.

name: Arnold Palmer
notes: Equal parts lemonade and unsweetened iced tea over ice. If the lemonade is very sweet, lean slightly toward more tea rather than adding lemon juice.

name: Salty Dog
notes: Salt only the outside rim of the highball so the salt does not fall into the drink. Otherwise it is vodka and grapefruit juice built over ice.

name: Greyhound
notes: Two parts grapefruit to one part vodka, built over ice with no rim. Fresh grapefruit juice makes a clear difference in a drink this simple.

name: Gin Fizz
notes: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup hard, strain over fresh ice in a highball, then add soda. The hard shake gives the drink a lively texture before the soda goes in.

name: Ramos Gin Fizz
notes: Dry shake first if using egg white, then shake a long time with ice to build foam. Strain into a collins glass with no ice and add the soda gently so the foam rises.

name: Sloe Gin Fizz
notes: Sloe gin brings its own sweetness, so this uses less syrup than a standard Gin Fizz. Shake, strain over ice in a highball, and top with soda.

name: Pimm's Cup
garnish: Cucumber ribbon, mint, orange and strawberry slices
notes: Build the Pimm's over ice, top with lemonade or ginger ale, and load it with cucumber, mint, orange and strawberry. The fresh fruit adds as much flavor as the liqueur.

name: Shandy
notes: Pour the lager first, tilting the glass to control the head, then add lemonade. The ratio is close to half and half, so adjust to taste.

name: Snakebite
notes: Pour the lager and hard cider in equal amounts into the highball over ice. Pour slowly, as both are carbonated and the head builds up quickly.

name: Black Velvet
notes: Pour the stout into the wine glass first, then top slowly with champagne. Let the foam settle between pours so it does not overflow.

name: Tequila Sunrise
notes: Build the tequila and orange juice over ice, then pour the grenadine gently so it sinks to the bottom. Do not stir; the gradient is the look of the drink.

name: Grasshopper
notes: Equal parts crème de cacao, green crème de menthe and cream. Shake hard with ice to aerate the cream, then strain into a chilled coupe.

name: Golden Cadillac
notes: Galliano replaces the crème de menthe of a Grasshopper, giving vanilla and anise instead of mint. Shake firmly and strain into a coupe with no ice.

name: Pink Squirrel
notes: Crème de noyaux brings the pink color and an almond-like flavor. Shake it with the crème de cacao and cream, then strain up into a chilled coupe.

name: Alexander
notes: Gin, crème de cacao and cream shaken hard and strained into a coupe. Grate fresh nutmeg over the top; pre-ground nutmeg lacks aroma.

name: Velvet Hammer
notes: Cointreau and white crème de cacao with cream and no base spirit. Shake hard and strain up; it tastes gentle but still contains two liqueurs.

name: Nutty Irishman
notes: Pour the Frangelico, Irish cream and heavy cream over ice in a rocks glass and give a quick stir. No shaking is needed for this build.

name: Toasted Almond
notes: Shake the vodka, amaretto, coffee liqueur and cream with ice, then strain into a rocks glass over fresh cubes. Shaking blends the cream fully.

name: Separator
notes: Brandy, coffee liqueur and cream shaken and strained into a coupe. It resembles a Brandy Alexander, but coffee liqueur takes the place of crème de cacao.

name: Chocolate Martini
notes: Shake vodka, crème de cacao and cream until very cold, then strain into a chilled martini glass. Add the chocolate shavings after the drink is poured.
